title: Orders of a rational section: independence of the generator and finiteness

source.place: Section 'The Weil divisor class associated to an invertible module' (section-c1): the paragraph before Tag 02SF (divisors-definition-order-vanishing-meromorphic), 'there exists a unit $u\in\mathcal O_{X,\xi}^*$ such that $s_\xi=us'_\xi$ ... $s/s_\xi$ is independent of the choice of $s_\xi$ up to multiplication by a unit' (clause 1), and Tag 02SG (divisors-lemma-divisor-meromorphic-locally-finite) with its proof (clause 2: on a nonempty open where $s$ generates $\mathcal L$ the order is $0$, and only the finitely many components of the complement remain), specialized to the smooth connected curve $C$, whose prime divisors are its closed points.

proof.text: *Independence of the generator.* Fix a closed point $P$. Since $e$ and $e'$ both generate the free rank-one $\mathcal O_{C,P}$-module $\mathcal L_P$ [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk], there is a unit $u\in\mathcal O_{C,P}^*$ with $e'=ue$. Thus $g'=gu^{-1}$ in $k(C)^*$. The normalized DVR valuation $v_P$ in the statement sends $u$ and $u^{-1}$ to $0$ (the exponent of a unit in its uniformizer factorization is $0$), so $v_P(g')=v_P(g)$.

source.place: Section 02SE, paragraph immediately before Definition 02SF: two generators differ by a unit, so the ratio of a meromorphic section to a generator is defined up to a unit

proof.text: *A nonzero rational section generates on a nonempty open.* Choose an open neighbourhood of the generic point $\eta$ on which $\mathcal L$ is free with generator $e$ [def-sc-invertible-module], then a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ inside it. Since $\eta$ is generic, it lies in $V$. The image of $e$ is a basis of $\mathcal L_\eta$ [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk], so $s=g e_\eta$ for some $g\in k(C)^*$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], write $g=a/b$ with $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$. The principal open $U=D(ab)\subseteq V$ is nonempty (it contains $\eta$), and both $a$ and $b$ are units on $U$. Hence $g$ and $g^{-1}$ are regular on $U$, and $s=(a/b)e$ is a generator of $\mathcal L|_U$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 02SG, first sentence: a nonzero meromorphic section generates the invertible module on a nonempty open; the affine fraction and principal-open construction makes this sentence explicit

proof.text: *Finite support.* For every closed point $P\in U$, the germ $s_P$ generates $\mathcal L_P$, so writing $s=g_P\lambda_P(e_P)$ for any generator $e_P$ gives $g_P\in\mathcal O_{C,P}^*$ and $v_P(g_P)=0$ by the normalized DVR valuation in the statement. Therefore the closed points with nonzero order lie in $Z=C\setminus U$. This is a proper closed subset of the integral curve $C$, since $\eta\in U$. If $Z$ contained a strict chain of two nonempty irreducible closed subsets, appending $C$ would give a chain of length two in $C$, contrary to $\dim C=1$ [def-sc-curves]; thus $\dim Z\le0$. Since $C$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-curves], [lem-sc-dim0-finite] gives that $Z$ is a finite set of closed points. The set of $P$ with nonzero order is a subset of this finite set.

source.place: Lemma 02SG, proof: all nonzero-order prime divisors lie outside the open where the section generates; specialization to a finite-type integral curve, with finite zero-dimensional closed subsets as in [lem-sc-dim0-finite]
